source: Confucius said: There are seventy-seven disciples who have studied with me and become proficient in the six arts. They are all people with extraordinary talents. Outstanding in virtue: Yan Yuan, Min Ziqian, Ran Boniu, Zhong Gong. Those who are good at handling political affairs: Ran You, Ji Lu. In terms of language: Zaiwo, Zigong. Articles on erudition: Ziyou, Zixia. Master Zhuan Sun was extreme, Zeng Shen was slow, Gao Chai was stupid, Zhong You was rude, and Yan Hui was often poor and had nothing. Duanmuci did not accept the mercy of fate and went into business, but his predictions on the market were often accurate. The people whom Confucius respected: in the Zhou Dynasty, it was Laozi; in the Wei Kingdom, it was Zang Boyu; in the Qi Kingdom, it was Yan Zhongping; in the Chu Kingdom, it was Laolaizi; in the Zheng Kingdom, it was Zichan; in the Lu Kingdom, it was Meng Gongchuo. He also often praised Zang Wenzhong, Liu Xiahui, Tongtan Bohua, and Jieshan Ziran. Confucius was born later than them and was not of the same era. Yan Hui was from the state of Lu, his courtesy name was Ziyuan. Thirty years younger than Confucius. Yan Yuan asked what benevolence was, and Confucius said: Restrain yourself and make your words and deeds conform to etiquette, and people in the world will praise you as a virtuous person. Confucius said: Yan Hui! What a virtuous person! He ate a small bamboo basket of rice, drank a ladle of water, and lived in a simple alley. Most people couldn't bear this kind of hardship, but Yan Hui didn't change his joy. When he was listening to my teachings, Yan Hui seemed like a stupid person. After class, I examined his private conversations and showed that he was able to express himself deliberately. Yan Hui was really not stupid. When you are employed, you will save the world; when you are not employed, you will hide your secrets. Only you and I have such an attitude towards life! Yan Hui was only twenty-nine years old, his hair turned completely white, and he died prematurely. Confucius cried very sadly and said: Since I had Yan Hui, the students have become closer and closer to me. Duke Ai of Lu asked: Who among the students is the best at learning? Confucius replied: There is a man named Yan Hui who had better learn from others and never transfer his anger to others and never make the same mistake again. Unfortunately, life was short, and after death, there are no such people anymore. Min Sun, also known as Ziqian, was fifteen years younger than Confucius. Confucius said: Min Ziqian is too filial! He serves his parents and obeys his brothers. Others praise him without any criticism. He does not want to be a retainer of a high official, and he does not want to receive a salary from an emperor. So he said: If someone calls me again, I will definitely flee to the north of Wenshui River. Ran Geng, courtesy name Boniu. Confucius thought he was virtuous. Boniu was suffering from an incurable disease. Confucius went to greet him, shook his hand from the window, and said: This is life! Such a good person got such a disease, what a fate! Ran Yong, courtesy name Zhong Gong. Zhong Gong asked how to handle political affairs. Confucius said: When going out to do things, be as courteous and courteous as receiving distinguished guests, and use the people as piously and cautiously as hosting a grand ceremony. In this way, no one will resent you if you serve in the feudal state of a prince, and no one will resent you if you serve in the home of a high official.
gold_target: Confucius identified seventy-seven disciples proficient in the six arts, categorizing them by virtue (Yan Yuan, Min Ziqian, Ran Boniu, Zhong Gong), political skill (Ran You, Ji Lu), eloquence (Zaiwo, Zigong), and erudition (Ziyou, Zixia). He noted individual traits: Zhuan Sun was extreme, Zeng Shen slow, Gao Chai stupid, Zhong You rude, and Yan Hui poor. Zigong, rejecting fate, became a successful merchant. Confucius respected figures like Laozi, Zang Boyu, Yan Zhongping, Laolaizi, Zichan, and Meng Gongchuo, and praised others from earlier eras. Yan Hui (Yan Yuan), thirty years younger than Confucius, was praised for virtue, living frugally without changing his joy. Confucius said he restrained himself to conform to etiquette, was not stupid, and shared a philosophy of serving when employed and hiding when not. Yan Hui died prematurely at twenty-nine, causing Confucius great grief. Duke Ai of Lu was told Yan Hui was the best learner, never transferring anger or repeating mistakes.

source: Confucius thought that Zhong Gong had achieved great achievements in virtue and said: Ran Yong, you can make him a high official like a senior official. Zhong Gong's father was a man of humble status. Confucius used an analogy and said: A mottled cow gives birth to a red calf with round and straight horns. Even if you don't want to use it as a sacrifice, will the gods of the mountains and rivers abandon it? Ran Qiu, also known as Zi You, was twenty-nine years younger than Confucius. As the head of Li family's retainers. Ji Kangzi asked Confucius: Is Ran Qiu virtuous? Confucius replied: There is a city with a thousand households and a fief with a hundred chariots. Ran Qiu can manage the military and political affairs there well. As for whether he is benevolent or not, I don't know. Ji Kangzi asked again: Is Zilu virtuous? Confucius replied: Just like Ran Qiu. Ran Qiu asked Confucius: Do you act immediately when you hear what you should do? Confucius replied: Act immediately. Zilu asked Confucius: When you hear something you should do, should you act immediately? Confucius replied: How can you act immediately when you hear something when your father and brothers are here? Zihua felt that this was strange and said in confusion: "I boldly ask, why do you ask the same question but get different answers?" Confucius replied: Ran Qiu was timid and worried, so I encouraged him. Zhong Yu has the courage of two people to do things, so I have to restrain him. Zhong Yuan, named Zi Lu, was from Bian. Nine years younger than Confucius. Zilu had a rough temperament, liked to show off his strength, had a strong ambition, and was straightforward. He wore a rooster-style hat and a sword decorated with boar skin. He once bullied Confucius. Confucius slowly induced him with ritual music. Later, Zilu dressed in Confucian clothes and brought a gift for apprenticeship. Through the recommendation of Confucius's students, Zilu asked to be Confucius's student. Zilu asked how to deal with political affairs. Confucius said: You must first set an example for the people, and then you can make the people work hard. Zilu asked for further explanation. Confucius said: Be persistent. Zilu asked: Does a gentleman value bravery? Confucius said: What a gentleman values ​​most is righteousness. A gentleman who has no choice but to be brave but does not uphold righteousness will become rebellious and rebellious. A villain who has no choice but to be brave but not uphold righteousness will become a robber. Zi Lu wanted to hear some truth, but he didn't act immediately, for fear of hearing another truth. Confucius said: The only person who can decide a case by just listening to one side's words is Zhong You! Zhong Yu advocates bravery more than I can use it, so it does not apply. People with a temperament like Zhongyou's will not end well. I'm afraid Zhong You is the only one who doesn't feel ashamed to stand next to people wearing fur coats while wearing a shabby robe made of tangled linen. Zhong Yuan's knowledge seems to have reached the main hall, but he has not yet been able to enter the inner room. Ji Kangzi asked: Is Zhong You virtuous? Confucius replied: A country with a thousand chariots can let him manage military and political affairs. As for whether he has benevolence, I don't know. Zilu liked to travel with Confucius and met hermits such as Changju, Jieyou, and an old man carrying farm tools. Zilu became Ji's retainer. Ji Sun asked Confucius: Can Zilu be said to be a retainer? Confucius replied: It can be said that he is a minister who is ready to fill his position. Zilu was appointed as the official of Pucheng and bid farewell to Confucius. Confucius said: There are many brave warriors in Pu Yi, and it is difficult to govern them. However, I tell you: if you are respectful and humble, you can control brave people; if you are generous and honest, you can bring everyone close to you; if you are respectful and honest and the society is quiet, you can use it to serve your superiors. At first, Duke Linggong of Wei had a favorite concubine named Nanzi.
gold_target: Min Ziqian, fifteen years younger, was deemed exceptionally filial, avoiding official service. Ran Boniu suffered an incurable disease; Confucius lamented his fate. Zhong Gong, asked about governance, was advised to be courteous and cautious; Confucius deemed him fit for high office despite his humble father. Ran Qiu, twenty-nine years younger, managed military affairs for the Ji family; Confucius encouraged his timidity. Zilu (Zhong You), nine years younger, was bold and straightforward, initially bullying Confucius but later becoming a disciple. Confucius taught him to prioritize righteousness over bravery, and he died in Wei during a rebellion, tying his hat before death.

source: King Wu was very happy, so he sent Zigong to Yue. The King of Yue cleared the road and went to the outskirts to greet Zigong. He personally drove his car to the residence where Zigong was staying and asked, "This is a remote and backward country. Why did the doctor humiliate his solemn status and come here?" Zigong replied: Now I have persuaded King Wu to rescue Lu and attack Qi. He wanted to do this but was afraid of Yue and said, "Wait until I capture Yue." Like this, it is inevitable to conquer the Yue Kingdom. Besides, it would be too clumsy to make people suspicious of someone without the intention to retaliate; it would be unsafe to have people know about it if he has the intention to seek revenge; it would be too dangerous to let people know about it before the matter has started. These three situations are the biggest disaster in getting things done. After hearing this, Gou Jian kowtowed to the ground and bowed again and said: I once overestimated my capabilities and went to war with Wu. I was besieged in Kuaiji. I hated him so much that my lips were parched day and night. I only wanted to fight to the death with the King of Wu. This is my wish. So he asked Zigong what to do. Zigong said: The king of Wu was ferocious and cruel, and the ministers could not bear it; the country fought many wars, which made it exhausted and decayed, and the soldiers could not bear it; the people resented the king, and there were internal disturbances among the ministers; Wu Zixu was killed for his remonstrances, and the chief minister came to power, complied with the fault of the king, and used it to protect his own selfish interests. This is a political manifestation of harming the country. Now if the king can really send troops to assist the king of Wu, appeal to his will, use heavy gold and treasures to win his favor, and honor him with humble words to show respect for him, he will definitely attack Qi. If that war cannot be won, it will be your great blessing. If he wins, he will definitely lead his troops to approach Jin. Please let me go north to meet the king of Jin and let him attack it together. This will definitely weaken the power of Wu. When all their elite troops were consumed in the Qi State, the heavy troops were restrained by the Jin State, and the king took advantage of its exhaustion to attack it, which would surely destroy the Wu State. The King of Yue was very happy and agreed to act according to the plan. He gave Zigong a hundred yi of gold, a precious sword, and two good spears. Zigong didn't accept it and left. Zigong reported back to the King of Wu and said: I solemnly told the King of Yue what you said. The King of Yue was very frightened and said: I am very unlucky. I lost my father when I was young. Five days later, Wen Zhong, a senior official from the State of Yue, kowtowed to the ground and said to the King of Wu: Gou Jian, the minister of the East China Sea Service, would like to send the envoy Wen Zhong to repair your subordinates and ask them to send greetings to the king. Now I heard privately that the king is going to launch an army of justice to attack the violent, support the weak and tyrannical Qi State and appease the Zhou royal family. I request to send out the entire army of 3,000 people in Yue State. Gou Jian requested to personally wear armor and carry sharp weapons, and was willing to risk the danger of arrows and stones in front. Therefore, Wen Zhong, a humble minister of the Yue Kingdom, was sent to present the treasures treasured by his ancestors, including twelve pieces of armor, axes, Qulu spears, and light swords, as gifts to the noble military officials. The King of Wu was very happy after hearing this and told Zigong what Wen Zhong had said: The King of Yue wants to follow me personally to attack Qi. Is that okay? Zigong replied: No. It is unethical to make someone else's country empty, mobilize all his troops, and ask his king to follow him on an expedition. You accept his gift and allow him to send his army without his king accompanying him. The king of Wu agreed and thanked the king of Yue. So King Wu mobilized the troops from nine counties to attack Qi. Zigong therefore left the state of Wu and went to the state of Jin. He said to the king of Jin: I heard that if you don't plan a strategy in advance, you can't cope with sudden changes, and if you don't manage the army well in advance, you can't defeat the enemy. Now the state of Qi and the state of Wu are about to go to war. If the state of Wu cannot win the war, the state of Yue will definitely take the opportunity to disrupt it; after winning the battle with the state of Qi, the king of Wu will definitely lead his army to approach the state of Jin. Jin was very panicked and said: What should we do? Zigong said: Prepare your weapons, recuperate your soldiers, and wait for the arrival of the Wu army. Jin Jun did as he said. Zigong left Jin and went to Lu. Sure enough, the King of Wu fought a battle with the Qi people in Ailing and defeated the Qi army. He captured seven generals' soldiers and refused to return home. Sure enough, he led his troops to approach the Jin state and met the Jin people in Huangchi. Wu and Jin were competing for supremacy. The Jin people attacked Wu and defeated the Wu army. When the King of Yue heard the news of the Wu army's disastrous defeat, he crossed the river to attack the state of Wu. He did not set up camp until he was seven miles away from the capital of the state of Wu. When King Wu heard the news, he left Jin and returned to Wu, where he fought with the Yue army in the Five Lakes area. Many battles failed, and even the city gate could not be defended. So the Vietnamese army surrounded the palace and killed King Wu Fucha and his minister. Three years after the destruction of the Wu State, the Yue State dominated the east. Therefore, Zigong's trip saved the state of Lu, disrupted the state of Qi, destroyed the state of Wu, made the state of Jin strong, and enabled the state of Yue to dominate. Zigong's mission caused corresponding changes in the situation of various countries. Within ten years, the situations of Qi, Lu, Wu, Jin, and Yue each changed. Zigong was good at hoarding rare things, buying at low prices and selling at high prices, and changing hands to make profits according to the supply and demand situation.
gold_target: Zaiwo, eloquent, questioned the three-year mourning period, suggesting one year sufficed; Confucius rebuked him for lacking benevolence. Zaiwo later died in a rebellion in Qi. Zigong, thirty-one years younger, was articulate and wealthy. Confucius compared him to a vessel and praised his humility. Zigong’s diplomatic mission saved Lu, disrupted Qi, destroyed Wu, strengthened Jin, and enabled Yue’s dominance, altering the balance of power among states.

source: He likes to promote the strengths of others and does not hide the faults of others. He once served as the prime minister of Lu and Wei, and his family fortune accumulated thousands of gold. He eventually died in Qi. Yan Yan was from the state of Wu and his courtesy name was Ziyou. Forty-five years younger than Confucius. After Ziyou received his profession, he served as the governor of Wucheng. Confucius passed by Wucheng and heard the sound of playing the harp and singing. Confucius smiled slightly and said: Why use a knife to kill a chicken? Ziyou: Once upon a time, I heard my husband say: Talented people who learn rituals and music will cultivate their benevolence and love the people; ordinary people who learn rituals and music will abide by laws and regulations and be easy to control. Confucius said to the accompanying students: Everyone, what Yan Yan said is correct. What I just said was just a joke. Confucius believed that Ziyou was familiar with articles and erudite. Bu Shang, courtesy name Zixia. Forty-four years younger than Confucius. Zixia asked: "The beautiful smile is charming and moving, the bright eyes are flowing and shining, and the pure white hair of the Buddha is dyed with brilliant literary colors. What do these three sentences mean?" Confucius replied: Painting must first have a pure white background, and then decorate the picture with color. Zixia said: Did the emergence of ritual and music come after benevolence and righteousness? Confucius said: Fortune teller, now I can discuss the Book of Songs with you. Zigong asked: Which one is stronger, master Zhuan Sun or the diviner? Confucius said: Master, it's a little too much, Shang, it's a little behind. Zigong said: Is Master Zhuan Sun any better? Confucius said: Excess and failure to catch up are equally imperfect. Confucius said to Zixia: You must aspire to be a talented and virtuous scholar, not a shallow and dishonest scholar. After the death of Confucius, Zixia settled in Hexi to teach students and became the teacher of Wei Wenhou. Zixia's son died, and he cried his eyes out. Master Zhuan Sun was a native of Chen State, his courtesy name was Zizhang. Forty-eight years younger than Confucius. Zizhang learned from Confucius how to obtain official salary. Confucius said: Listen more to what others say, and do not make rash comments about unsolved problems. Others should be cautious when speaking out, so that you can make fewer mistakes; watch more people's actions, and don't act rashly about unsolved problems. Others should act cautiously, which can reduce regrets. The fewer mistakes you make in your words and the fewer regrets in your actions, the official salary you seek will be contained in it. One day Zizhang followed Confucius and was besieged between the states of Chen and Cai. Zizhang asked how to make everything work. Confucius said: If you are honest and trustworthy in your words and sincere and respectful in your actions, it will work even in the southern barbarians and Beidi; if you are not loyal and trustworthy in your words and sincere and respectful in your actions, will it work even in your own hometown? When standing, the words "loyalty, trust and reverence" appear before your eyes; when sitting in the car, the words "loyalty, trust and reverence" are hung on the crossbar in front of the car. Once you reach this point, it will work everywhere. Zizhang wrote these words on the big belt around his waist. Zizhang asked: What can a scholar do to be called enlightened? Confucius said: What do you mean by mastery? Zizhang replied: "You must have a good reputation among the princes' states, and you must also have a good reputation in the families of ministers and officials." Confucius said: This is reputation, not understanding. The so-called understanding should be upright and righteous, consider other people's words, observe other people's expressions, and always think about humility and concession. In this way, you will be able to gain access in the states of princes and the fiefdoms of ministers and officials.
gold_target: Ziyou, forty-five years younger, governed Wucheng with music and ritual; Confucius joked about using a “knife to kill a chicken” but later praised him. Zixia, forty-four years younger, discussed the Book of Songs with Confucius, who noted his slight deficiency. After Confucius’s death, Zixia taught in Hexi. Zizhang, forty-eight years younger, learned about gaining office through caution and about achieving success through loyalty and respect. Zeng Shen, forty-six years younger, understood filial piety and wrote the Book of Filial Piety.

source: The reputation mentioned above seems to be pursuing benevolence, but in actual actions it violates benevolence. You have to deal with it calmly. There is no doubt that such a person will definitely gain fame in the states of princes and the fiefdoms of ministers and officials. Zeng Shen was a native of Nanwucheng, named Liaoyu, and was forty-six years younger than Confucius. Confucius thought that he could understand filial piety, so he taught him his studies. He wrote a "Book of Filial Piety". He died in the state of Lu. Tantai Mieming was a native of Wucheng, named Ziyu. Thirty-nine years younger than Confucius. His body and appearance were ugly. He wanted to serve Confucius, but Confucius thought that he had low qualifications. After studying as a teacher, he devoted himself to self-cultivation practice when he returned home. He dealt with things openly and honestly, and did not take evil paths. It was not for official business and he never met with officials or officials. He traveled south to the Yangtze River, and there were three hundred students who followed him. He was flawless in acquiring, giving, abandoning, and pursuing, and his reputation spread to the princes in all directions. Confucius heard these things and said: If I judge people by words only, my judgment of Jaeyu is wrong; if I judge people by appearance alone, my judgment of Ziyu is wrong. The words are not neat and the characters are cheap. Thirty years younger than Confucius. Confucius talked about Mi Zi Jian and said: Zi Jian is really a gentleman! If there are no gentlemen in the state of Lu, where did this person learn such good character? Zi Jian was appointed as Shanfu's local governor. He came back and reported to Confucius, saying: "There are five people in this place who are more talented than me. They taught me how to govern the people." Confucius said: What a pity! The areas that are not managed uniformly are too small. If the areas that are managed are large, it will be almost the same. Yuan Xian, courtesy name Zisi. Zisi asked what shame was. Confucius said: If the country's politics are clear, you can be an official and receive a salary, but you can't see trees. The country's politics are dark, and it is a shame to be an official and receive a salary but not be able to stand alone. Zisi said: If competitiveness, self-praising, resentment, and greed are not revealed, can it be regarded as benevolence? Confucius said: It can be said to be commendable. Whether it can be regarded as benevolence, I don't know. After Confucius passed away, Yuan Xian went to live in seclusion in a low-lying place with water and overgrown weeds. Zigong became the Prime Minister of Wei State, and there was a continuous stream of carriages and horses when he went out, pushing through the thick weeds, and came to a remote, simple and dilapidated hut to visit Yuan Xian. Yuan Xian tidied up his shabby clothes and met Zigong. Seeing this, Zigong felt ashamed for him and said, "Are you embarrassed?" Yuan Xian replied: I have heard that those who have no property are called poverty, and those who have learned principles but cannot implement them are called embarrassment. Like me, poverty is not embarrassment. Zigong felt very ashamed and left unhappy. He felt ashamed for his whole life that he had said the wrong thing this time. Gongye Chang was a native of Qi State, with the courtesy name Zichang. Confucius said: If Gong Ye is the leader, you can marry your daughter to him. Even if he is in prison, it is not his fault.

source: The king of Nanyue, Wei Tuo, was from Zhending and his surname was Zhao. The Qin State annexed the six countries, captured and pacified Yang Yue, established Guilin, Nanhai and Xiangjun, and resettled the people who had committed crimes and migrated to these places, and lived together with the Yue people for thirteen years. Wei Tuo was appointed as the magistrate of Longchuan County in Nanhai County during the Qin Dynasty. During the second year of Qin Dynasty, Ren Xiao, the captain of Nanhai County, fell ill and was about to die. He summoned Zhao Tuo, the commander of Longchuan, and said to him: I heard that Chen Sheng and others had launched a rebellion, and that the Qin Dynasty was pursuing cruel and unjust policies, and the people of the world were resentful of this. Xiang Yu, Liu Bang, Chen Sheng, Wu Guang, etc. all gathered people in their respective states and counties at the same time, formed armies, and fought for the world like tigers. The Central Plains region was in turmoil, and it was unknown when peace would be restored. Heroes betrayed the Qin Dynasty and opposed each other. Nanhai County is remote and remote, and I am afraid that the bandit army will invade the land. When I attack here, I want to mobilize the army to cut off the newly built road to the Central Plains. I have taken precautions in advance and wait for the changes in the princes. It happens that I am seriously ill. Let’s talk about Panyu. There are dangerous mountains behind us to rely on, and there is the sea as a barrier to the south. It is thousands of miles away from east to west. We have some Central Plains people to assist us. We can also be the lord of a state and establish a country. There is no one among the governors of Nanhai County who is worthy of me to study these things with him, so I have summoned you to tell you these things. Ren Xiao immediately issued an appointment document to Zhao Tuo, asking him to act on behalf of Nanhai County. After Ren Xiao died, Zhao Tuo sent a message to Hengpu, Yangshan, and Huangxiguan, saying: The bandit army is coming, so we must quickly cut off the road, gather the army, and defend ourselves. Zhao Tuo took this opportunity to gradually use the law to kill the officials installed by the Qin Dynasty, and use his cronies as acting governors. After the Qin Dynasty was destroyed, Zhao Tuo attacked and annexed Guilin and Xiangjun, and established himself as King Wu of South Vietnam. Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty had already pacified the world. Because the people in the Central Plains were tired and miserable, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty spared Zhao Tuo and did not kill him. In the eleventh year of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty, he sent Lu Jia to South Vietnam and ordered Zhao Tuo to inherit his title of King of South Vietnam, make an agreement with him, exchange envoys, and let him coordinate Baiyue so that they can live in harmony and not become a scourge to the south of the Han Dynasty. South Vietnam borders Changsha to the north. During the post-Gao period, officials from relevant departments requested that South Vietnam be prohibited from purchasing ironware in border markets. Zhao Tuo said: Emperor Gao made me the king of South Vietnam, and the two sides exchanged envoys and supplies. Now Gao Hou listens to the opinions of the slanderers, treats the barbarians as aliens, and cuts off the source of the artifacts we need. This must be the idea of ​​King Changsha. He wants to follow the Han Dynasty in the Central Plains, eliminate South Vietnam, double as the king of South Vietnam, and establish his own merits. So Zhao Tuo took advantage of the title and called himself Emperor Wu of Nanyue. He sent troops to attack the border cities of Changsha and defeated several counties before leaving.
gold_target: The king of Nanyue, Wei Tuo (Zhao Tuo), was from Zhending. During the Qin dynasty, after conquering the six states, the Qin annexed Yang Yue, establishing Guilin, Nanhai, and Xiangjun, and resettled criminals there to live with the Yue people for thirteen years. Zhao Tuo served as the magistrate of Longchuan County in Nanhai. In the second year of the Qin dynasty, Ren Xiao, the captain of Nanhai, fell ill. He summoned Zhao Tuo and explained that with Chen Sheng’s rebellion and the Qin’s cruel policies, the Central Plains were in chaos. He noted that Nanhai was remote and could be defended by mountains and sea, and suggested Zhao Tuo could establish a state. Ren Xiao appointed Zhao Tuo as acting captain. After Ren Xiao’s death, Zhao Tuo cut off roads, gathered troops, killed Qin-appointed officials, and replaced them with his cronies. Following the Qin’s fall, he annexed Guilin and Xiangjun and declared himself King Wu of Nanyue. Emperor Gaozu of Han, due to the people’s exhaustion, spared Zhao Tuo. In the eleventh year of Gaozu, he sent Lu Jia to confirm Zhao Tuo as King of Nanyue, with an agreement for envoys and harmony with Baiyue. During Empress Lü’s reign, officials banned ironware trade with Nanyue. Zhao Tuo suspected King Changsha’s influence, declared himself Emperor Wu of Nanyue, and attacked Changsha’s border cities. Empress Lü sent General Zhou Zao to attack, but heat and illness halted the army. After her death, the Han stopped. Zhao Tuo expanded his territory to over 10,000 miles, bribing Minyue, Xiou, and Luoyue, and acted as an emperor.

In the hot and humid climate, most of the soldiers became seriously ill, making it impossible for the army to cross Yangshan Mountains. More than a year later, Queen Gao died, and the Han army stopped attacking. Therefore, Zhao Tuo relied on his army to show off his power on the border, and bribed Minyue, Xiou and Luoyue with property to make them all belong to South Vietnam, making his territory more than 10,000 miles long from east to west. Zhao Tuo actually rode in Huangwu Zuohu's chariot and issued orders as the emperor, which was equal to the status of the Han Dynasty. In the first year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, when the emperor had just ruled the world, he sent envoys to the princes and the rulers of the barbarians from all over the world to inform them of his intention to come to Beijing from Dai to ascend the throne, and to let them know the emperor's saintly virtues. So for the tomb of Zhao Tuo's parents in Zhending, a tomb guard was set up, and sacrifices were held on time every year. His cousins ​​were also summoned, and they were given honorable official positions and generous rewards to show their favor. The emperor ordered Prime Minister Chen Ping to recommend people who could be sent as envoys to South Vietnam. Chen Ping said that Lu Jia, a native of Haochou, had served as envoys to South Vietnam many times during the late emperor's reign. The emperor summoned Lu Jia, appointed him Taizhong doctor, and went to South Vietnam as an envoy. He took the opportunity to blame Zhao Tuo for proclaiming himself emperor and not sending an envoy to report to the emperor. When Lu Jia arrived in South Vietnam, the South Vietnamese king Zhao was particularly frightened and wrote an apology to the emperor, saying: The barbarian chief husband Chen Tuo used to isolate and discriminate against South Vietnam. I secretly suspected that the king of Changsha was a slanderous minister. I also heard in this distant place that the high queen killed Zhao Tuo's clan and dug and burned the graves of his ancestors. Therefore, he abandoned himself and invaded the border area of ​​​​Changsha. Moreover, in the low and humid land in the south, among the barbarians, Minyue in the east only had thousands of people, but they called their ruler king; in the west, naked countries like Xiou and Luoyue also had to call themselves kings. So I arrogantly stole the emperor's title to comfort myself. How dare I report this to the emperor! Zhao Tuo kowtowed deeply and apologized, saying that he would remain a vassal minister of the Han Dynasty for a long time and abide by his duty to pay tribute to the emperor. So Zhao Tuo issued an order to the whole country, saying: I heard that two heroes cannot coexist, and two sages cannot live together in the same world. The emperor of the Han Dynasty was a wise emperor. From now on, I will get rid of the imperial system and will no longer ride in Huangwu Zuohu's car. Lu Jia returned to Beijing to report the matter, and Emperor Wen of Han was very happy. Continuing to the era of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Zhao Tuo professed his vassalage to the Han Dynasty and sent people to Chang'an to meet the emperor in the spring and autumn. However, in South Vietnam, Zhao Tuo always stole the title of emperor. He only became king when he sent envoys to meet the emperor, and accepted the emperor's orders just like the princes. In the fourth year of Jianyuan, Zhao Tuo died. Zhao Tuo's grandson Zhao Hu became the king of South Vietnam.
gold_target: In the first year of Emperor Wen of Han, the emperor honored Zhao Tuo’s parents’ tomb and his cousins. He sent Lu Jia to rebuke Zhao Tuo for claiming the emperor title. Zhao Tuo apologized, citing fear of King Changsha and the queen’s actions, and claimed he used the title for self-comfort among barbarians. He pledged vassalage to Han, removed imperial trappings, and continued as a vassal. During Emperor Jing’s era, Zhao Tuo outwardly submitted but secretly kept the emperor title. He died in the fourth year of Jianyuan, succeeded by his grandson Zhao Hu.

source: At this time, King Ying of Minyue launched a war to attack the border towns of South Vietnam. Zhao Hu sent people to write to the Emperor of Han, saying: South Vietnam and Minyue are both vassals of the Han Dynasty and cannot send troops to attack each other without permission. Now that Fujian and Yue have invaded me, I dare not send troops to fight. I hope that the emperor will issue an edict to deal with this matter. So the emperor praised the South Vietnamese for their loyal behavior and abiding by their duties and covenants, sent troops for them, and sent two generals to attack Minyue. Before the Han army crossed the Yangshan Mountains, Yu Shan, the younger brother of the King of Minyue, killed Ying and surrendered to the Han Dynasty, thus stopping the crusade. The emperor of the Han Dynasty sent Zhuang Zhu to explain the court's intentions to the King of Nanyue. Zhao Hu kowtowed deeply and said: The emperor sent troops to attack Fujian and Yue for me. Even if I die, I can't repay the emperor's kindness! Zhao Hu sent Prince Yingqi to the court to serve as a bodyguard. He then said to Zhuang Zhu: The country has just been invaded by the enemy. Please leave first. Zhao Hu was preparing his bags day and night to go to the capital to meet the emperor. After Zhuang Zhu left, his ministers admonished Zhao Hujin and said: The Han Dynasty sent troops to kill Ying, and they also used this action to warn South Vietnam. Moreover, the late king once said in the past that when serving the emperor, one only hopes not to be rude. The most important thing is not to go to the emperor just because you like to listen to the good words of the messenger. If you go to court to see the emperor, you will not be able to come back. This is a situation of national subjugation. So Zhao Hu used illness as an excuse and did not go to see the Emperor of Han in the end. More than ten years later, Zhao Huzhen became seriously ill, and Prince Yingqi asked to return to the country. When Zhao Hu died, he was given the posthumous title of King Wen. After Ying Qi Dai was established as the King of Nanyue, he hid the seal of Emperor Wu of his ancestor. When Yingqi went to Chang'an to serve as a guard, he took a daughter from Handan's family as his wife and gave birth to a son named Zhao Xing. When he ascended the throne and became king, he wrote to the Emperor of the Han Dynasty, requesting that his wife Xi be made the queen and Zhao Xing be the prince. The Han Dynasty repeatedly sent envoys to tactfully advise Ying Qi to go to the emperor. Ying Qi liked to kill people arbitrarily and was afraid that if he went to the capital to worship the emperor, he would be forced to follow the laws of the mainland and implement the laws of the Han Dynasty. Therefore, he used illness as an excuse to not go to the emperor and only sent his son Cigong to the capital to serve as a guard. When Yingqi died, he was given the posthumous title of King Ming. Prince Zhao Xingdai was established as the King of Nanyue, and his mother became the Queen Mother. When the Queen Mother was not married to Yingqi as her concubine, she had committed adultery with Anguo Shaoji, a native of Baling. After Yingqi's death, in the fourth year of Yuanding, the Han Dynasty sent Anguo Shaoji to persuade the King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother to go to Beijing to worship the emperor like the princes in the interior. He ordered the debaters to admonish the official Zhongjun and others to publicize this idea, and asked the warrior Wei Chen and others to assist him where they were insufficient. Guard Lu Bode led his troops to garrison in Guiyang, waiting for the envoy.
gold_target: Zhao Hu faced an attack from Minyue’s King Ying. He requested Han intervention, and Emperor Wu sent troops, leading to Ying’s death. Zhao Hu thanked the emperor but, advised by ministers, avoided visiting the capital, fearing captivity. He died as King Wen. His son Yingqi, who had married a woman from Handan and fathered Zhao Xing, became king. Yingqi hid his grandfather’s emperor seal, refused to visit the capital due to fear of Han laws, and died as King Ming. Zhao Xing succeeded, with his mother as queen mother.

source: The King of Nanyue is young, and the Queen Mother is from the Central Plains. She once committed adultery with Anguo Shaoji. This time Anguo Shaoji came to serve as an envoy and committed adultery with her again. Most people in South Vietnam knew about this, and most of them did not rely on the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother was afraid of unrest and wanted to rely on the power of the Han Dynasty. She repeatedly persuaded the King of Nanyue and his ministers to request to belong to the Han Dynasty. So he sent a letter to the emperor through an envoy, requesting that the princes in the interior should meet with the emperor once every three years and remove the border barriers. So the emperor agreed to their request and gave the silver seal to Lu Jia, the prime minister of South Vietnam, and also gave the official seals such as internal history, lieutenant, and master, and the rest of the official positions were placed by South Vietnam himself. They abolished their previous punishments of tattoos and torture, and used the laws of the Han Dynasty to compare with the princes in the interior. The envoys stayed to pacify South Vietnam. The King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother packed their belongings and valuables in preparation for going to Beijing to meet the Emperor. Lu Jia, the prime minister of South Vietnam, was very old and had assisted three kings. There were more than 70 officials and officials in his clan. The men all married the princess's wives, and the women married the princes and their brothers' clan members. They were related by marriage to the King of Qin in Cangwu County. His position in South Vietnam is very prominent, and the South Vietnamese people trust him. Many people have become his cronies, surpassing the King of South Vietnam in terms of popular support. The King of Nanyue wanted to write to the emperor. He repeatedly suggested that the king give up this move, but the King of Nanyue did not listen. He had the idea of ​​​​treason against the King of Nanyue, and repeatedly excused himself from meeting the Han Dynasty envoys due to illness. The envoys paid great attention to Lu Jia's words and deeds, but due to the situation, they did not execute Lu Jia. The King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother were also afraid that Lu Jia would be the first to attack, so they arranged a banquet and planned to use the power of the Han Dynasty envoys to kill Lu Jia and others. At the banquet, the envoys all faced east, the Queen Mother faced south, the king faced north, and Prime Minister Lu Jia and the ministers all faced west, sitting and drinking with them. Lu Jia's younger brother was a general and led his troops to wait outside the palace. While drinking, the Queen Mother said to Lu Jia: It is in the interests of the country that South Vietnam belongs to the Han Dynasty, but Prime Minister, you complain that this is not good. Why? The Queen Mother wanted to anger the Han Dynasty envoy. The envoy hesitated and did not dare to kill Lu Jia. Lu Jia saw that the people around him were not his cronies, so he stood up and walked out. The queen mother got angry and wanted to hit Lu Jia with a spear, but the king stopped her. Lu Jia went out, divided some of his brother's soldiers, and arranged them around his residence. He refused to meet the king and the envoy because of his illness. Lu Jia secretly prepared to launch a rebellion with his ministers. The King of Nanyue had no intention of killing Lu Jia. Lu Jia knew this, so he did not launch a rebellion for several months. The Queen Mother had engaged in promiscuous behavior and no one in the South Vietnam country would join her. She wanted to kill Lu Jia alone, but she was unable to do it. The Emperor heard that Lu Jia disobeyed the King of Nanyue. The King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother were weak and could not control Lu Jia, and the envoys were timid and incapable of decision-making.
gold_target: The queen mother, who had previously committed adultery with Anguo Shaoji, sought to submit to Han. Emperor Wu sent Anguo Shaoji to persuade them. The young king and queen mother agreed to become vassals, but Prime Minister Lu Jia, who had served three kings and held great influence, opposed. He feared losing power and plotted rebellion. At a banquet, the queen mother tried to provoke the Han envoy to kill Lu Jia, but the envoy hesitated. Lu Jia left, gathered troops, and refused to meet the king. The queen mother’s efforts failed.

source: In the autumn of the fifth year of Yuan Ding, Weiwei Lu Bode became General Fubo and led his troops out of Guiyang and went straight down to the Huishui River; Lieutenant Yang Pu, the Lord Commander, became the general of the building and ship, left Yuzhang and went straight down to Hengpu; two people who had returned to the Han Dynasty and were made marquises A South Vietnamese man became General Ge Chuan and General Xia Li and led his troops out of Lingling. Then one army went straight to Lishui and the other to Cangwu. He asked Chiyihou to use the sinners of Bashu to mobilize Yelang's soldiers and go straight to the Zoke River. In the end, they all met up in Panyu. In the winter of the sixth year of Yuanding, General Lou Chuan led his elite troops to first capture Xunshan, then broke through Shimen, paid the warships and grain of South Vietnam, took the opportunity to advance forward, defeated the vanguard of South Vietnam, and led tens of thousands of troops to wait for General Fubo. Therefore, only more than a thousand people joined General Louchuan, so they moved forward together. General Lou Chuan was in front and fought straight to Panyu. Zhao Jiande and Lu Jia were both defending in the city. General Louchuan chose a favorable place to garrison in the southeast of Panyu; General Fubo garrisoned in the northwest of Panyu. Just when it was dark, General Lou Chuan attacked and defeated the South Vietnamese and set fire to Panyu City. The South Vietnamese have heard the name of General Fubo in normal times, but now that it's dark, they don't know how many troops he has. General Fubo set up camp, sent envoys to summon those who surrendered, gave them official seals, and then sent them back to recruit others. General Lou Chuan fought hard and burned the enemy, but drove the rebels into General Fubo's camp to surrender. At dawn, all the enemy soldiers in the city surrendered to General Fubo. Lu Jia and Zhao Jiande had fled into the sea with hundreds of their subordinates at night and took a boat to the west. General Fubo took the opportunity to ask the South Vietnamese nobles who had surrendered, and then he knew Lu Jia's whereabouts and sent people to hunt him down. Su Hong, a former school captain who is now an officer of General Fubo, captured Zhao Jiande and was named Chang Haihou; Nanyue native Lang Guan Duji captured Lu Jia and was named Lincai Marquis. Zhao Guang, King of Cangwu, had the same surname as the King of Nanyue. Hearing that the Han Dynasty troops had arrived, the Jieyang County magistrate named Ding of Nanyue decided to join the Han Dynasty. Weng, the governor of Guilin County in Nanyue, informed Ou Luo to surrender to the Han Dynasty. They were all sealed. Before the troops of General Ge Chuan and General Xia Li, as well as the Yelang army so called mobilized by Marquis Chiyi, had arrived, South Vietnam had been pacified. So the Han Dynasty established nine counties here. General Fubo increased the number of fiefs, and General Louchuan's army broke through the enemy's strong defense, so he was granted the title of General Lianghou. After Zhao Tuo first became king, the Kingdom of Nanyue was destroyed for five generations, a total of ninety-three years. Tai Shigong said: Wei Tuo became the king of Nanyue because of Ren Xiao's promotion and persuasion. Just as the Han Dynasty was initially stabilized, he was made a prince. Longluhou led his troops to attack South Vietnam. They encountered a hot and humid climate. Many of the soldiers were infected with diseases and were unable to march, which made Zhao Tuo even more proud.
gold_target: The emperor sent Han Qianqiu with 2,000 troops to South Vietnam. Lu Jia rebelled, killed the king, queen mother, and Han envoys, and installed Zhao Jiande as king. Han Qianqiu’s army was ambushed and destroyed. The emperor then launched a large-scale attack in the fifth year of Yuanding, with generals Lu Bode, Yang Pu, and others leading forces from multiple directions. In the sixth year, Yang Pu’s troops captured Panyu, and Lu Bode’s forces accepted surrenders. Lu Jia and Zhao Jiande fled by sea but were captured. South Vietnam was pacified, and the Han established nine counties. The kingdom lasted five generations for ninety-three years. The historian notes that Zhao Tuo’s rise was due to Ren Xiao, and the kingdom’s fall stemmed from internal conflicts and Lu Jia’s actions.

source: General Wei Qing was a native of Pingyang County. His father Zheng Ji served as a minor official in the county and served in the family of Pingyang Marquis Cao Shou. He had an affair with Pingyang Marquis's concubine Wei Wei and gave birth to Wei Qing. Wei Qing's half-brother is called Wei Changzi, and his half-sister is called Wei Zifu. Wei Zifu was favored by Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty in Princess Pingyang's family, so he pretended to be surnamed Wei. Wei Qing, whose given name is Zhongqing. The eldest son of Wei changed his surname to Changjun. Changjun's mother is Wei Yu. Wei's eldest daughter is called Wei Ru, her second daughter is Wei Shaoji, and her third daughter is Wei Zifu. Later, Wei Zifu's younger brothers Bu and Guang both pretended to be surnamed Wei. Wei Qing was a servant of the Hou family in Pingyang. When he was a child, he returned to his father Zheng Ji's house, and his father asked him to shepherd sheep. Zheng Ji's sons from his first marriage all treated him as a slave, not as a brother. Wei Qing once followed someone to the living room of Ganquan Palace. A prisoner with an iron shackle around his neck came to Wei Qing and said, "You are a noble man. You will be a high official and a marquis in the future!" Wei Qing smiled and said, "I was born of a slave. I would be satisfied if I didn't get beaten or scolded by others. How could I think of becoming a marquis?" When Wei Qing grew up, he became a cavalryman of the Pingyang Hou family and often followed Princess Pingyang. In the spring of the second year of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Wei Qing's sister Wei Zifu entered the palace and was favored by Emperor Wu. Queen Chen Ajiao is the daughter of Liu Piao, the eldest princess of Tangyi. She has no sons and is jealous. The eldest princess heard that Wei Zifu was favored by Emperor Wu and was pregnant. She was jealous of her and sent people to arrest Wei Qing. At that time, Wei Qing was serving in Jianzhang Palace and was not yet famous. The eldest princess arrested and imprisoned Wei Qing and wanted to kill him. Wei Qing's friend Qi Lang Gongsun Ao and some strong men snatched him out. For this reason, Wei Qing did not die. When Emperor Wu heard the news, he summoned Wei Qing and appointed him as the supervisor of Jian Zhang, with the title of Shizhong. Together with his half-brothers, they all received high status, and the emperor's rewards for them accumulated as much as a thousand pieces of gold in a few days. Wei Ru became the wife of Grand Servant Sun He. It turned out that Wei Shaoer had an affair with Chen Zhang, so Emperor Wu summoned Chen Zhang and made him a noble person. As a result, Gongsun Ao became more and more prominent. Wei Zifu became Emperor Wu's wife. Wei Qing was promoted to Dazhong doctor. In the fifth year of Yuanguang, Wei Qing served as the general of cavalry and attacked the Xiongnu, marching out of the fortress from Shanggu; Sun He, the imperial servant, served as the general of light chariots and marched out of the fortress from Yunzhong; Gongsun Ao, the Dazhong doctor, served as the general of cavalry and marched out from Daijun; Wei Wei Li Guang served as the general of heroic cavalry and marched out of the fortress from Yanmen; each army had ten thousand cavalry. Wei Qing led his troops to Fucheng and killed hundreds of enemies.
gold_target: Wei Qing, a native of Pingyang County, was the illegitimate son of Zheng Ji and a concubine of the Pingyang Marquis household. His half-sister Wei Zifu gained favor with Emperor Wu of Han, leading Wei Qing to adopt the surname Wei. As a youth, he served as a servant and shepherd, enduring mistreatment from his half-brothers. A prisoner once prophesied his future nobility, but Wei Qing dismissed it. He later became a cavalryman for the Pingyang Marquis. When Wei Zifu entered the palace and became pregnant, Empress Chen, jealous, attempted to kill Wei Qing. His friend Gongsun Ao rescued him, and Emperor Wu subsequently appointed Wei Qing as a palace supervisor, elevating his status. Wei Zifu later became empress, and Wei Qing was promoted to Dazhong doctor.

He once served Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, and when Emperor Wu of the Han came to the throne for eight years, he became a general officer and garrisoned in Mayi. gold_target: In 129 BCE, Wei Qing led a cavalry attack on the Xiongnu, achieving modest success. Subsequent campaigns saw him capture the Henan region, driving out Xiongnu kings and establishing Shuofang Commandery. For these victories, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changping. Further campaigns against the Xiongnu resulted in significant victories, including the capture of King Youxian's forces and vast numbers of livestock. Emperor Wu granted Wei Qing additional households and enfeoffed his sons as marquises, though Wei Qing humbly declined, crediting the emperor and his officers.

source: In addition, many of the petty officials and soldiers under the Hussars General Huo Qubing served as officials and received rewards. The hussar general is a man of few words, silent, courageous and courageous. Emperor Wu once wanted to teach Sun Tzu and Wu Qi the art of war. He replied: In war, it only depends on the policy and strategy. There is no need to learn ancient war art. Emperor Wu built a mansion for him and asked General Hussar to take a look. He replied: The Huns have not been eliminated yet, so they have no intention of considering private matters. From then on, Emperor Wu valued and favored Hussar General Huo Qubing more. However, Huo Qubing had been serving the emperor in the palace since he was a boy, receiving dignitaries, but he did not know how to show sympathy to the soldiers. When he went to war, the emperor sent his eunuchs to give him dozens of carts of food. When he came back, there was a lot of leftover rice and meat thrown away on the carts, and some of his soldiers were starving. When he was fighting outside the wall, the soldiers were short of food, and some were so hungry that they could not stand up, while the hussar generals were still drawing pitches and playing football games. Most of what he does is like this. General Wei Qing was kind-hearted and had a spirit of compromise. He pleased the emperor with his tolerance and gentleness, but no one in the world praised him. General Hussar passed away three years after his attack on the Xiongnu in the fourth year of Yuanshou, that is, in the sixth year of Yuanshou. Emperor Wu was very sad about his death, and dispatched the armored troops from the five border counties to form a formation from Chang'an to Maoling, so that the outside of the tomb built by Huo Qubing would look like praying for the mountains. He was given a posthumous title, combining the two principles of bravery and territorial expansion, and called him Marquis Jinghuan. Huo Qubing's son Yan succeeded the title of Champion Marquis. Huo Shen was young and named Zihou. The emperor liked him and hoped to appoint him as a general when he grew up. Six years later, in the first year of Yuanfeng, Huo Huan died, and the emperor gave him the posthumous title of Aihou. He had no sons, so his descendants were cut off and the feudal state was abolished. Since the death of General Hussar, the general's eldest son, the Houwei couple of Yichun, lost their marquis title for breaking the law. Five years later, the two younger brothers of the Wei couple, the Marquis of Yin'an Wei Buyi and the Marquis of Fagan Weideng, both lost their marquis titles because they were guilty of insufficient gold and insufficient weight. Two years after losing the marquis, the feudal state of the champion marquis was abolished.
gold_target: Wei Qing's nephew, Huo Qubing, emerged as a brilliant commander, earning the title of Champion Marquis for his daring raids. Huo Qubing's campaigns were marked by deep penetrations into Xiongnu territory, capturing kings and vast numbers of enemies. He became increasingly favored by the emperor, eventually matching Wei Qing in rank and power. Huo Qubing famously declined a mansion, stating, "The Xiongnu have not yet been eliminated, so I have no intention of considering private matters." However, he was known for his lack of concern for his soldiers' welfare, often discarding food while they starved. After Huo Qubing's death, Wei Qing's influence waned. Wei Qing died four years later, and his descendants lost their titles due to legal infractions. The text concludes with a list of Wei Qing's and Huo Qubing's subordinates, many of whom became generals or marquises. The historian Sima Qian notes that Wei Qing, despite his nobility, refrained from recruiting scholars, fearing the emperor's displeasure, a principle Huo Qubing also followed.

source: Sima Ranju is a descendant of Tian Wan. I hope the king can give him a try. So Qi Jinggong summoned Rangju and discussed military and state affairs with him. After discussing with him, Qi Jinggong was very happy and immediately appointed him as a general and ordered him to lead troops to resist the armies of Yan and Jin. Rangju said: "I am of a humble status. The king promoted me from the common people and placed me above the officials. The soldiers will not obey and the people will not trust me. If a person has little qualifications, authority cannot be established. I hope the king can send a minister who is favored by the king and respected by the people to supervise the army. That will be enough." So Qi Jinggong agreed to his request and sent Zhuang Jia to supervise the army. After Rang Ju bid farewell to Jinggong, she made an agreement with Zhuang Jia: "We will meet at the camp gate at noon tomorrow." The next day, Rang Ju rushed to the military gate first and set up a wooden watch and a clepsydra to wait for Zhuang Jia. However, Zhuang Jia has always been arrogant and dignified. He thinks that he is leading his own army and he is the supervisor of the army, so he is not particularly anxious. His relatives and friends bid farewell to him and invited him to drink wine. It was already noon, but Zhuang Jia had not yet arrived. Rangju knocked down the wooden watch, broke the clepsydra, entered the military camp, inspected the camp, organized the army, and issued various rules and orders. By the time he finished his deployment, it was already dusk when Zhuang Jia arrived. Rangju said: Why are you late even if you agree on the time? Zhuang Jia apologized and explained: My friends and relatives sent me off, so I was delayed. Rangju said: As a general, you should forget about your family from the moment you receive an order. When you come to the army and issue the prescribed orders, you should forget about personal friendships. When you beat the drum and march, you should forget about your own life when the battle is urgent. Now that the enemy's invasion has penetrated deep into the country, there is unrest in the country, the soldiers have been exposed on the frontline battlefield, and there is no place to hide, the monarch has trouble sleeping and eating sweetly, and the lives of the people in the country are hanging on you, so why talk about farewell! So he called the military judge and asked: According to military law, what is said about people who are late for the agreed time? The answer was: He should be beheaded. Zhuang Jia was very frightened and sent Pegasus to report to Qi Jinggong and ask him to rescue him. Not long after the messenger left, but before he could return, Zhuang Jia was beheaded and paraded in front of the three armies. The entire army was shocked and frightened. After a long time, the envoy sent by Qi Jinggong came to pardon Zhuang Jia with the festival talisman. The carriages and horses galloped straight into the military camp. Rangju said: "Generals are in the army, and they do not have to accept some of the king's orders." He also asked the military judge: "What is the military law stipulating that driving a chariot and horse galloping in the military camp?" The military judge said: He should be beheaded. The messenger was extremely frightened. Rangju said: The king's envoy cannot be beheaded. So he beheaded the servants of the messenger, cut off the wooden carriage on the left side, killed the horses driving the carriage on the left side, and paraded in front of the three armies. He asked the envoy to go back and report to Qi Jinggong, and then set off.
gold_target: Sima Ranju, a descendant of Tian Wan, was recommended by Yan Ying to Qi Jinggong during a crisis when Jin and Yan attacked Qi. Despite his humble status, Ranju’s literary and military talents impressed the king, who appointed him general. Ranju requested a trusted minister, Zhuang Jia, to supervise the army. They agreed to meet at the camp gate at noon. Ranju arrived early and set up timing devices, but Zhuang Jia, delayed by farewell feasts, arrived at dusk. Ranju condemned his lateness, citing that a general must forsake family, friendships, and personal safety in war. He executed Zhuang Jia under military law, shocking the army.

source: Lu Buwei was a big businessman in Yangzhai. He traveled around, buying at low prices and selling at high prices, so he accumulated a fortune worth thousands of gold. He was not rich in carriages, horses and daily necessities, and his life was difficult and very unhappy. Lu Buwei went to Handan to do business. After seeing Zi Chu, he felt very fond of him and said: Zi Chu is like a rare commodity that can be hoarded. So he went to visit Zi Chu and persuaded him: I can expand your family. Zi Chu smiled and said: "For now, let's expand your own family first, and then come and expand mine!" Lu Buwei said: "You don't understand. My family has to wait for your family to grow before it can grow." Zi Chu knew what Lu Buwei meant, so he sat him down together and had an in-depth conversation. Lu Buwei said: The King of Qin is old, and Lord An Guo was made the crown prince. I heard privately that Lord An Guo dotes on Mrs. Huayang very much. Mrs. Huayang has no son, so only Mrs. Huayang can choose the prince. Now you have more than twenty brothers, and you are ranked in the middle. You are not favored by the King of Qin and have been left as a hostage in the vassal states for a long time. Even if the King of Qin dies and An Guojun succeeds to the throne, you should not expect to compete with your eldest brother and other brothers who are by the King of Qin's side sooner or later. Zichu said: That's true, but what should we do? Lu Buwei said: "You are very poor and embarrassed, and you are living here as a guest. Although I, Lu Buwei, am not rich, I am willing to spend thousands of dollars to lobby for you to the west, serve Lord An Guo and Mrs. Huayang, and ask them to make you the crown prince. Zichu then kowtowed and thanked him and said: If your plan comes true, I am willing to entrust the land of Qin to share it with you. Lu Buwei then gave 500 gold to Zichu for daily life and making friends with guests. He also took 500 gold to buy rare things. He took these things with him and went west to the Qin State to lobby. He first paid a visit to Mrs. Huayang's sister and dedicated all the things he brought to Mrs. Huayang. By the way, I mentioned that Zi Chu was smart and virtuous, and he made friends with princes and guests all over the world. He often said, "I, Zi Chu, regard my wife as the same as the sky. I cry day and night and miss the prince and his wife." Madame was very happy. Lu Buwei took the opportunity and asked Mrs. Huayang's sister to persuade Mrs. Huayang: "I heard that if you use your beauty to serve others, once your beauty fades, your favor will also decrease."
gold_target: Lu Buwei, a wealthy merchant from Yangzhai, amassed a fortune through low-cost buying and high-price selling. source: Mengchangjun's surname is Tian Mingwen. Tian Wen's father is Jingguo Jun Tian Ying. Tian Ying is the youngest son of King Qi Wei and the younger brother of King Qi Xuan's concubine. Tian Ying has been in power since he was King Wei. He once led troops with Chenghou Zou Ji and Tian Ji to rescue South Korea and attack Wei. Later, Chenghou and Tian Ji competed for the favor of King Qi and had a deep rift. As a result, Chenghou betrayed Tian Ji. Tian Ji was very frightened, so he launched a surprise attack on the city on the border of Qi. He failed to capture it and ran away. At this time, King Wei of Qi passed away and King Xuan came to the throne. King Xuan knew that it was Chenghou who framed Tian Ji, so he recalled Tian Ji and made him a general. In the second year of King Xuan of Qi, Tian Ji, Sun Bin and Tian Ying attacked the state of Wei, defeated the state of Wei in Maling, captured the prince Shen of the state of Wei, and killed the general Pang Juan of the state of Wei. In the seventh year of King Xuan, Tian Ying was ordered to go to South Korea and Wei as an envoy. After some of his activities, South Korea and Wei were surrendered to Qi. Tian Ying accompanied Han Zhaohou and King Wei Hui to meet with King Qi Xuan in Dong'anan. The three countries formed an alliance and signed a treaty before leaving. The next year, King Xuan met with King Hui of Liang again in Zhendi. This year, King Hui of Liang passed away. In the ninth year of King Xuan's reign, Tian Ying became prime minister of Qi. King Xuan of Qi and King Xiang of Wei respected each other as kings at the Xuzhou League. After King Chu Wei learned about this incident, he was very angry with Tian Ying and thought that he was the one who planned it. The next year, Chu attacked Qi and defeated the Qi army in Xuzhou, so they sent people to hunt down Tian Ying. Tian Ying sent Zhang Chou to persuade King Chu Wei, and King Chu Wei finally gave up. Tian Ying served as prime minister of Qi for eleven years. King Xuan died and King Min came to the throne. Three years after King Min came to the throne, he granted Tian Ying the title of "Xue Yi". At first, Tian Ying had more than forty sons. One of his concubines gave birth to a son named Wen. Tian Wen was born on May 5th. Tian Ying told Tian Wen's mother: Don't raise him. But Tian Wen's mother still secretly raised him. When he grew up, his mother introduced Tian Wen to Tian Ying through Tian Wen's brother. When Tian Ying saw the child, he angrily said to his mother: I asked you to throw this child away, but you dared to feed him. Why? Before Tian Wen's mother could answer, Tian Wen immediately kowtowed and then asked Tian Ying: "Why are you not allowed to raise a child born in May?" Tian Ying replied: A child born in May will be disadvantageous to his parents when he grows to be as tall as the door. Tian Wen said: Is human destiny granted by God? Or is it awarded by the portal? Tian Ying didn't know how to answer, so he remained silent. Tian Wen continued: If it is granted by God, why should you worry? If it is granted by the portal, then as long as the portal is raised, who can grow so tall! Tian Ying was speechless and scolded: "Stop talking!" After a long time, Tian Wen took the opportunity to ask his father: "What is the name of your son's son?" Tian Ying replied: "Call me grandson." Tian Wen then asked: What is the name of your grandson’s grandson? Tian Ying replied: "My name is Great-grandson." Tian Wen asked again: What is the name of your great-great-grandson's grandson? Tian Ying said: I don’t know anymore. Tian Wen said: You have held great power and served as the prime minister of Qi. You have been kings for three generations. However, the territory of Qi has not expanded, but your private family has accumulated tens of thousands of gold, and there is not a single virtuous person under your family.

He had over forty sons, but Tian Wen was born on May 5th, a date considered inauspicious. Tian Ying ordered the child abandoned, but his mother secretly raised him. When Tian Wen grew up, he confronted his father, arguing that fate was determined by heaven, not by the doorframe, and criticized Tian Ying for accumulating wealth while neglecting the state's welfare. Impressed, Tian Ying made Tian Wen his heir.

At this time, a guest, Su Dai, said to him: I came out this morning and saw a puppet man and a clay puppet talking. The puppet man said: As soon as it rains, you will collapse. The earth puppet said: I was born from the earth. Even if it collapses, I will return to the earth. If it really rains and the water rushes towards you, I don’t know where it will take you. Today's Qin State is a country as fierce as a tiger or a wolf. If you insist on going there, if you cannot come back, will you not be laughed at by the local puppets? After hearing this, Lord Mengchang realized the truth and stopped preparing for the trip. In the twenty-fifth year of King Min of Qi, he finally sent Lord Mengchang to Qin. King Zhao of Qin immediately appointed Lord Mengchang as the prime minister of Qin.

Lord Mengchang knew that the situation was critical, so he sent someone to see King Zhao's concubine to ask for help. The concubine made a condition and said: I hope to get Lord Mengchang's white fox fur. When Lord Mengchang came, he brought with him a white fox fur, which was worth thousands of gold. There was no second one in the world. When he arrived in Qin, he presented it to King Zhao, and there was no other fur. Lord Mengchang was worried about this matter. He asked all the guests, but no one could think of a solution. There was a man who was not very capable but could steal things in dog skins. He said: I can get that white fox fur. So that night, he disguised himself as a dog, went into the warehouse of the Qin Palace, took out the fox white fur that was presented to King Zhao, and took it back and presented it to King Zhao's concubine. After getting the concubine, she interceded with King Zhao on behalf of Lord Mengchang, and King Zhao released Lord Mengchang. After Mengchangjun was released, he immediately fled by express train, changed his exit certificate, changed his name and escaped from the city pass. We arrived at Hangu Pass at midnight. King Zhao regretted releasing Lord Mengchang and sent people to look for him again. When he found that he had escaped, he immediately sent people to chase him. Mengchangjun and his party arrived at Hangu Pass. According to the customs law, guests can only be let out when the rooster crows. Mengchangjun was worried that his pursuers would arrive. Among the guests, there was a person who was of low rank but could imitate the rooster's crow. As soon as he imitated the rooster's crow, the nearby chickens also crowed, and he immediately showed his documents and escaped from Hangu Pass. After about a meal after leaving the pass, Qin's pursuers arrived at Hangu Pass, but fell behind Lord Mengchang, so they had to go back. When Lord Mengchang accepted these two people as guests, the guests all felt ashamed and disgraced. When Lord Mengchang suffered a disaster in Qin, he finally relied on these two people to escape. From then on, the guests all admired Mengchangjun's approach of recruiting guests regardless of their status. Lord Mengchang passed by the State of Zhao, and Lord Pingyuan of the State of Zhao treated him as a distinguished guest. When the people of Zhao heard about Mengchang's talents, they all came out to watch and see him. When they saw him, they all laughed and said: "I thought Mengchang was a tall man, but now I see him, he is just a skinny man." Mengchangjun was very angry after hearing these teasing words. The guests who were traveling with him jumped out of the car, killed hundreds of people, and left after destroying a county. King Qi Min felt guilty for sending Lord Mengchang to Qin. After Lord Mengchang returned to Qi State, the King of Qi made him prime minister of Qi State and in charge of state affairs. Lord Mengchang resented Qin and planned to unite South Korea and Wei to attack Qin on the grounds that Qi had helped South Korea and Wei attack Chu. To this end, he borrowed weapons and rations from the Western Zhou Dynasty.
gold_target: King Zhao of Qin, hearing of Lord Mengchang's virtue, invited him to Qin and appointed him prime minister. However, officials warned that Lord Mengchang, being a Qi noble, would prioritize Qi's interests, so King Zhao imprisoned him. Lord Mengchang's concubine demanded his white fox fur as a bribe for her intercession. A guest skilled in thievery disguised himself as a dog, stole the fur from the palace, and gave it to the concubine, who secured Lord Mengchang's release. As he fled, another guest imitated a rooster's crow to open the Hangu Pass gates before pursuers arrived. Though initially ashamed of these lowly guests, Lord Mengchang's reliance on them earned admiration for his inclusive recruitment.

source: On behalf of the Western Zhou Dynasty, Su said to Lord Mengchang: You used the troops of Qi to help Han and Wei attack Chu for nine years, and gained the area north of Wan and Ye. As a result, Han and Wei became stronger. Now if you attack Qin, it will further strengthen the power of Han and Wei. If South Korea and Wei have no worries from Chu in the south, and no troubles from Qin in the north, then Qi will be in danger. When Korea and Wei become stronger, they will despise Qi and fear Qin. I really feel uneasy about this situation for you. It is better for you to let the Western Zhou Dynasty have a deep friendship with Qin State. You should not attack Qin State and do not borrow weapons and food. You send your army to Hangu Pass but do not attack. Let the Western Zhou Dynasty tell King Zhao of Qin your feelings and say that Duke Xue will definitely not attack Qin to strengthen the power of Han and Wei. His purpose in attacking Qin was just to ask the king to instruct Chu to cede the Eastern Kingdom to Qi, and to ask you to release King Huai of Chu to reach a reconciliation. You asked the Western Zhou Dynasty to use this method to benefit Qin. Qin could not be attacked and used Chu's territory to protect itself. Qin must want to do this. If the King of Chu could be released, he would definitely be grateful to the State of Qi. The Qi State will naturally become stronger and stronger after acquiring the Dong Kingdom, and Xue Yi will be free from worries for generations. Qin will not be overly weakened, and it is located to the west of South Korea and Wei. South Korea and Wei must rely on Qi. After hearing this, Lord Mengchang immediately said: "Okay." So Han and Wei were asked to congratulate Qin, which prevented a military disaster. Qi, Han, and Wei no longer sent troops to attack, and Qi stopped borrowing weapons and rations from the Western Zhou Dynasty. At this time, King Huai of Chu had already arrived in Qin, and Qin detained him, so Lord Mengchang must ask Qin to release him. But Qin did not do this. When Mengchang Jun was the prime minister of Qi, his attendant Wei Zi went to collect the tax from the feudal city for him. He made three trips back and forth, but he never got the tax back once. Lord Mengchang asked him what was the reason for this, and Wei Zi replied: There is a virtuous man. I donated the tax to him privately in your name, so I did not take it back. After hearing this, Lord Mengchang became angry and dismissed Wei Zi. A few years later, someone spread rumors about Lord Mengchang to King Min of Qi, saying that Lord Mengchang was about to launch a rebellion. When Tian Junjia kidnapped King Min, King Min suspected that it was Master Mengchang who planned it, and fled to avoid disaster. The sage who had received food as a gift from Wei Zi heard about this and wrote to King Min to state that Lord Mengchang would not cause rebellion and asked for his own life as a guarantee. He then cut his neck and committed suicide at the gate of the palace to prove Lord Mengchang's innocence. King Min was shocked, so he investigated and inquired about the actual situation. As expected, Lord Mengchang had no rebellion conspiracy, so he recalled Lord Mengchang. Lord Mengchang therefore excused himself from illness and asked to resign and return to Xue Yi to retire. King Min agreed to his request. After that, Qin's fugitive general Lu Li came to Qi to serve as Qi's prime minister. He wanted to put Su Dai in trouble. Su Dai said to Lord Mengchang: Zhou Zui was extremely loyal to the King of Qi, but the King of Qi expelled him and listened to the advice of his relatives and made Lu Li the prime minister. The reason was that he planned to unite with Qin.
gold_target: Later, Lord Mengchang became Qi's prime minister and planned to attack Qin with Han and Wei. Su Dai advised him to avoid strengthening Han and Wei, instead using the Western Zhou to negotiate with Qin for Chu's eastern territory and the release of King Huai of Chu. Lord Mengchang agreed, averting war. When dismissed as prime minister due to slander, he retired to Xue Yi. After Qin's general Lu Li became Qi's prime minister, Lord Mengchang, following Su Dai's advice, marched north to secure alliances, causing Lu Li to flee. When King Qi Min grew proud and sought to eliminate him, Lord Mengchang fled to Wei, became prime minister, and allied with Qin and Zhao to attack Qi, leading to King Min's death. King Xiang of Qi later reconciled with Lord Mengchang, who remained neutral among the states. After his death, his sons fought over the title, and Qi and Wei destroyed Xue Yi, ending his lineage.
